answer: Each identity claims one mesa bench and locks a 65-credit bond. It files one thread in the atlas register: dimensions, cart count, and tally. An auditor recomputes tonnage from volume times the atlas mesa density table and checks the thread against the tally. A mismatch, reused dimensions, or shared bench burns the bond. The first pays 31; the kth pays 31+5(k-1), so the 1000th pays 5026. One thousand fakes pay 2,528,500 plus 65,000 locked; an honest operator pays 31 once and recovers the bond. A rented-bench ring fails: its log carries its owner's key and its thread repeats another count.
